traceability.evidence: Rule implementation: src/rules/valid-req-reference.ts implements deep requirement validation: - Reads story files and extracts requirement IDs via regex /REQ-[A-Z0-9-]+/ (function loadAndCacheRequirements) - Validates @req lines against the extracted IDs (validateReqLine -> resolveStoryAndRequirements -> checkRequirementExists) - Supports @story and @supports annotations for story path resolution (handleAnnotationLine, parseImplementsLine, validateImplementsLine) - Caches requirement IDs per story file in a Map to avoid re-reading the same file multiple times per ESLint run (reqCache in programListener, loadAndCacheRequirements) - Performs safe path validation and project-boundary checks (validateAndResolveStoryPath, rejects path traversal and absolute paths; ensures resolved path stays under cwd) - Provides clear, specific error messages via meta.messages: `reqMissing: "Requirement '{{reqId}}' not found in '{{storyPath}}'"` and `invalidPath: "Invalid story path '{{storyPath}}'"` - Wires the rule into ESLint through create() returning a Program listener (programListener) that processes all comments for @story/@req/@supports annotations,Story linkage in rule code: - Top-level JSDoc on src/rules/valid-req-reference.ts explicitly references this story and its requirements: - @story docs/stories/010.0-DEV-DEEP-VALIDATION.story.md - @req REQ-DEEP-PARSE, REQ-DEEP-MATCH, REQ-DEEP-CACHE, REQ-DEEP-PATH - Additional functions (extractStoryPath, loadAndCacheRequirements, checkRequirementExists, validateReqLine, processCommentLines, programListener, create) reference 010.0 for parsing, matching and caching responsibilities, aligning with REQ-DEEP-* entries in the story,Tests for this story: tests/rules/valid-req-reference.test.ts - File header: - `Tests for: docs/stories/010.0-DEV-DEEP-VALIDATION.story.md` - @story docs/stories/010.0-DEV-DEEP-VALIDATION.story.md - @req REQ-DEEP-PARSE plus 007.0 error-reporting requirements - Valid cases (demonstrating successful deep validation across formats and structures): - `[REQ-DEEP-PARSE] valid requirement reference existing in story file` using: `// @story docs/stories/001.0-DEV-PLUGIN-SETUP.story.md` + `// @req REQ-PLUGIN-STRUCTURE` Verified against docs/stories/001.0-DEV-PLUGIN-SETUP.story.md, which contains the REQ-PLUGIN-STRUCTURE requirement. - `[REQ-DEEP-BULLET] valid bullet list requirement existing in bullet story fixture` using: `// @story tests/fixtures/story_bullet.md` + `// @req REQ-BULLET-LIST` and tests/fixtures/story_bullet.md where the requirement appears as a bullet list item: `- REQ-BULLET-LIST - a requirement in bullet list format`. - `[REQ-DEEP-IMPLEMENTS]` tests validating @supports multi-story semantics (integration with 010.2 story): - Single @supports line with multiple requirements in story_multi_a.md - Two @supports lines targeting story_multi_a.md and story_multi_b.md, both containing REQ-SHARED-ID plus file-specific IDs. Fixtures story_multi_a.md and story_multi_b.md each define these IDs in bullet lists, proving deep validation works per-file and supports shared IDs across multiple story files.,Negative test coverage (core validation, error reporting, and path handling): - Missing requirement in an otherwise valid story file: - `[REQ-DEEP-MATCH] missing requirement in story file` with `// @story docs/stories/001.0-DEV-PLUGIN-SETUP.story.md` + `// @req REQ-NON-EXISTENT` expects error: { messageId: 'reqMissing', data: { reqId: 'REQ-NON-EXISTENT', storyPath: 'docs/stories/001.0-DEV-PLUGIN-SETUP.story.md' } } - Path traversal and absolute-path protections for @story: - `../docs/stories/001.0-DEV-PLUGIN-SETUP.story.md` → error with messageId 'invalidPath'. - `/absolute/path/.../001.0-DEV-PLUGIN-SETUP.story.md` → error with messageId 'invalidPath'. - Bullet-list negative case: - `[REQ-DEEP-BULLET] missing bullet list requirement in bullet story fixture` using REQ-MISSING-BULLET against story_bullet.md: expected reqMissing error, proving deep check fails when ID isn’t present even in bullet format. - @supports negative cases (multi-story integration): - Missing requirement on @supports line (`// @supports tests/fixtures/story_multi_a.md REQ-NOT-IN-A`) triggers reqMissing with appropriate data. - Path traversal on @supports storyPath (`../tests/fixtures/story_multi_a.md`) triggers invalidPath, showing consistent error handling for both @story and @supports paths.,Test execution evidence: - npm test -- --verbose output shows: - "Valid Req Reference Rule (Story 010.0-DEV-DEEP-VALIDATION)" suite executed and all tests passed. - Detailed entries: - Valid tests: `[REQ-DEEP-PARSE] valid requirement reference existing in story file`, `[REQ-DEEP-BULLET] valid bullet list requirement existing in bullet story fixture`, `[REQ-DEEP-IMPLEMENTS]` scenarios. - Invalid tests: `[REQ-DEEP-MATCH] missing requirement in story file`, path traversal / absolute path cases, bullet-list-missing case, and @supports traversal case. - Overall Jest summary: 38 test suites passed, including the valid-req-reference suite; 290 tests passed in total, confirming the behavior is tested and stable.,Caching and performance behavior (REQ-DEEP-CACHE & performance notes): - src/rules/valid-req-reference.ts: - programListener initializes `const reqCache = new Map<string, Set>();` once per linted file. - loadAndCacheRequirements checks the map and only calls fs.readFileSync when the story file path is not yet cached: ```ts if (!reqCache.has(resolvedStoryPath)) { try { const content = fs.readFileSync(resolvedStoryPath, "utf8"); const found = new Set(); const regex = /REQ-[A-Z0-9-]+/g; ... reqCache.set(resolvedStoryPath, found); } catch { reqCache.set(resolvedStoryPath, new Set()); } } ``` - This ensures that, within a single ESLint run for a given file, each referenced story file is parsed at most once, satisfying the story’s requirement to avoid repeated parsing on every validation and providing graceful handling of read errors by caching an empty set without throwing.,Error handling and user experience (REQ-DEEP-ERROR & acceptance criteria): - Specific, contextual error messages are defined in rule meta.messages and used consistently: - reqMissing: includes both the missing requirement ID and the associated story path in the message template, e.g., "Requirement 'REQ-NON-EXISTENT' not found in 'docs/stories/001.0-DEV-PLUGIN-SETUP.story.md'". - invalidPath: includes the problematic storyPath value, identifying path traversal or absolute paths. - Tests in tests/rules/valid-req-reference.test.ts assert both messageIds and data payloads, proving that errors are clear, specific, and aligned with Story 007.0 error-reporting requirements. - loadAndCacheRequirements wraps fs.readFileSync in a try/catch and falls back to an empty requirement set on errors, preventing rule crashes on malformed/unreadable files and ensuring the linter behavior is graceful.,Integration with existing plugin architecture and rules (Integration acceptance criterion): - src/index.ts includes "valid-req-reference" in RULE_NAMES and dynamically loads it, ensuring it is part of the plugin’s exported rules. - TRACEABILITY_RULE_SEVERITIES marks "traceability/valid-req-reference" with severity 'error', and traceability.configs.recommended/strict include it, so the rule runs alongside existing rules like valid-story-reference and valid-annotation-format. - README.md lists `traceability/valid-req-reference` in the Available Rules section with description: "Validates that `@req` references point to existing requirement IDs.", clearly surfacing the rule to users. - user-docs/api-reference.md documents `traceability/valid-req-reference` with a description, default severity, and an example showing a @story/@req pair, and also references that deep requirement checking (for @req and @supports) is handled by this rule in the surrounding documentation for valid-annotation-format, demonstrating documented behavior and intended usage.,Support for various requirement formats and story structures (Quality Standards acceptance criterion & REQ-DEEP-FORMAT/SECTION): - Extraction strategy in loadAndCacheRequirements scans the entire markdown file with a generic `REQ-...` regex, independent of section titles, list styling, or formatting; this naturally supports: - Explicit requirement lines (e.g., in docs/stories/001.0-DEV-PLUGIN-SETUP.story.md Requirements section) where IDs like REQ-PLUGIN-STRUCTURE appear. - Bullet-list requirements in tests/fixtures/story_bullet.md (e.g., `- REQ-BULLET-LIST - a requirement in bullet list format`). - Multi-file reuse and per-story scoping in story_multi_a.md and story_multi_b.md, where bullet-list requirements and shared IDs are validated separately per file. - Because requirements are detected anywhere they appear in the markdown content (without assuming specific section headings), the rule inherently supports different story file layouts (Requirements section, Acceptance Criteria checklists, other headings) as long as they contain recognizable REQ- identifiers.
traceability.notes: Based on the implementation of src/rules/valid-req-reference.ts, its comprehensive tests in tests/rules/valid-req-reference.test.ts, successful Jest execution, and user-facing documentation in README.md and user-docs/api-reference.md, Story docs/stories/010.0-DEV-DEEP-VALIDATION.story.md is fully implemented. The rule validates that @req IDs exist in the referenced story files (including @supports-based multi-story usage), handles multiple story file structures and requirement formats (plain text, bullet lists, multi-file scoping), integrates with the plugin’s existing rules and configs, provides clear contextual error messages, uses caching to avoid repeated parsing within a run, and has documented behavior and examples. All acceptance criteria are satisfied by concrete, tested behavior in the current codebase.
